defect.visual_evidence: Continuous bright solder joining two adjacent fine-pitch pads.

hypotheses.text: Stencil wear is increasing deposited solder volume, causing bridging between fine-pitch pads.
Reflow peak temperature drifted upward after work order WO-388 (profile change), causing excess solder flow and bridging.
Elevated room humidity is slowing flux activation, leading to solder bridging.
A shift change to operator OP-17 increased variability in manual touch-up, causing bridging.

D1.text: Team: Priya R. · Quality Engineer, Sree Electronics (fictional) (lead) [complaint C-2026-031], SMT process engineer for Line 2 [PFMEA row 14], and the reflow maintenance technician who executed WO-388 [WO-388].

D2.text: Hoshino Denso (fictional) reported solder bridging on product ECU-PCB-7, lot L2611, affecting 14 of 500 units shipped [complaint C-2026-031]. Vision inspection of the returned unit confirmed a continuous bright solder bridge joining two adjacent fine-pitch pads, classified major severity at 86% confidence [Chart: defect photo annotation].

D3.text: Lots L2609, L2610, L2611, L2612, L2613 and L2614 from Line 2 are placed on hold pending disposition [Control plan item 6]. These lots were produced during the window when the reflow profile on Line 2 was out of specification following WO-388 [PFMEA row 14].

citations.label: Control plan item 6
citations.quote: Reflow peak temperature profile verification is required after any reflow profile change work order.

citations.label: PFMEA row 14
citations.quote: Reflow peak temperature out of profile window is a listed cause of solder bridging on fine-pitch pads.

D4.text: Root cause: reflow peak temperature on Line 2 drifted upward after profile change work order WO-388, pushing solder past liquidus for longer than specified and causing bridging between adjacent fine-pitch pads [PFMEA row 14]. This cause was verified with a Welch t-test comparing defect lots against good lots, p < 0.01, with a mean effect of +8.2 °C peak temperature in defect lots [Chart: reflow peak temp by lot]. The condition escaped detection because the post-change profile verification required after WO-388 was left in status profile_verification_pending and was never completed before production resumed [WO-388].

citations.label: PFMEA row 14
citations.quote: Reflow peak temperature out of profile window is a listed cause of solder bridging on fine-pitch pads.

D5.text: Permanent corrective action: re-qualify the Line 2 reflow profile to bring peak temperature back within the 250 °C specification limit and complete the profile verification step before resuming production [PFMEA row 14]. Work order WO-412 is raised to execute and sign off this re-qualification [WO-388].

D6.text: Implementation will be validated by re-running the reflow profile verification required under WO-388 and confirming peak temperature is within specification on three consecutive lots before the hold is released [Control plan item 6]. Effectiveness will be checked by re-testing the H2 comparison (defect lots vs good lots) and confirming no statistically significant temperature difference remains [Chart: reflow peak temp by lot].

citations.label: Control plan item 6
citations.quote: Reflow peak temperature profile verification is required after any reflow profile change work order.

D7.text: PFMEA row 14 is updated to flag post-change profile verification as a mandatory, blocking step rather than an advisory one [PFMEA row 14]. Control plan item 6 is updated to require sign-off evidence of profile verification before a line may resume production after any reflow profile change work order [Control plan item 6].

D8.text: The cross-functional team closed this 8D within the customer's 10-working-day requirement and the corrective actions are tracked to closure under CAPA-0142 [complaint C-2026-031]. Team contributions from quality, process engineering and maintenance are acknowledged [WO-388].
